item.subject: science
item.stem: Meera's mother keeps a block of jaggery near the hot stove, and after some time it starts turning soft and syrupy at its melting point. Which statement best explains why heating a solid like jaggery or ice can make it melt, and why the melting point is used to identify this change?

options.A: Heating pushes the particles closer together until they stop moving, and the melting point is the temperature at which particles stop vibrating.
options.B: Heating makes the particles vibrate more vigorously until they can leave their fixed positions, so the solid becomes liquid; the melting point is the specific temperature (at atmospheric pressure) at which this change begins, so it can be used to identify it.
options.C: Heating turns the solid particles into gas particles straight away, and the melting point is the temperature at which the solid evaporates.
options.D: Heating changes the particles into a different substance, and the melting point is just a number chosen from a table for each material.
